The first public release. A real Android emulator on a Selkies desktop, so an app can be installed, driven and broken without an APK ever touching a phone.

## ✨ Added

- The **real Android emulator**, the same AVD Android Studio starts, headless on a [Selkies](https://github.com/selkies-project/selkies) desktop. The screen arrives over WebRTC, hardware-encoded on the box's own GPU rather than smeared through a framebuffer diff.
- **Android 16, API 36, `google_apis`, x86_64.** The newest level on purpose: it is the strictest, and `google_apis` carries Play services and a real DocumentsUI, which is the SAF folder picker an app asks for a folder with.
- **`adb` over the network.** Connect with `adb connect <container-ip>:5555` and Android Studio treats it as an ordinary device. The emulator's own adb binds to loopback, so a forwarder inside the container hands the port to it.
- **Doze on demand**, which is the point of a real AVD over a container: `sk doze on` unplugs the battery first, because a device that believes it is charging refuses to go idle and reports success anyway.
- **`sk`, a helper on the container's terminal:** `sk list`, `sk install`, `sk push`, `sk doze` and `sk shell`.
- **A read-only share, mirrored onto the device** under `Download/share`, where the stock Files app and the SAF picker both find it. An APK dropped into the share from anywhere on the network can be installed by tapping it on the phone. The mirror has a size cap and refuses rather than truncates, because a mirror that copies only some of a folder is worse than one that says it stopped.
- **An Unraid template** ([`templates/strawknight.xml`](templates/strawknight.xml)) that puts the container on its own address, so no port mapping is needed.
- **The image is published**, so it can be pulled rather than built:

  ```
  docker pull ghcr.io/junkerderprovinz/strawknight:latest
  ```

  `amd64` only, and deliberately: the emulator runs an x86_64 system image with KVM, so an arm64 image would have nothing to run on it.

## ⚡ Improved

- The emulator window is **kept on screen**. On the first working build it opened at `y = -551` on a 768-pixel desktop, leaving sixty visible pixels, which from a browser is indistinguishable from an emulator that never started. Selkies also resizes the desktop to the browser window, so a one-off placement would not have held.
- A stale AVD is **moved aside rather than silently broken**. Raising the API level leaves an existing device pointing at a system image that is no longer installed; the boot script notices, renames it, says in the log that everything on it is gone with it, and builds a fresh one.
- The container **does not restart on its own**. An emulator is a virtual machine and holds its memory whether anybody is testing or not, about 6 GB idle with no app installed.
- The **desktop hint fits any window**. Selkies resizes the desktop to whatever the browser window is, so the wallpaper is fitted rather than cropped and the leftover is filled with the same colour, instead of the mark being cut in half at one size and repeated at another.

## Notes

**`PUID` and `PGID` are not optional.** They decide who owns `/config`, and they have to match the user that owns the directory on the host. Get them wrong and the emulator cannot write into its own AVD; the container then reports `A snapshot operation is pending and timeout has expired`, which reads like a corrupt device and is a permission bit.

No Community Applications listing and no Docker Hub mirror yet. It needs `/dev/kvm`; without it the emulator does not start and the log says so in as many words rather than leaving a black rectangle.
